requirements.title: Optional output validation skip (option enabled)
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦
  (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N),
      Builds t →
        ∀ (m : CountMarking N),
          Enabled t m →
            ∀ (d : List N),
              (∀ (p : N), Produced d p → OutputArc t p) → ∃ m', F t m d m') ∧
    (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (d : List N),
        on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x x_1 ↦
          ∀ (p : N), Produced d p → OutputArc t p) ∧
      ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N),
        ¬Builds t → ∀ (m : N → ℕ) (d : List N) (m' : N → ℕ), ¬F t m d m'
requirements.scope: an executor that offers the option, with the option enabled
reading: For every transition t that builds, whatever its output spec (an And, an Xor, or a single Place or ForwardInput leaf), every marking m at which t is enabled and every deposit d that writes only output places of t:
some firing of t from m deposits d.
Every firing of every transition deposits only in output places of the transition.
A transition that does not build never fires.
quotes: *While* the option is enabled, the executor *shall* deposit the tokens an action wrote without validating them against the transition's output spec.
The skip covers the whole spec, its `Place` and `ForwardInput` leaves included: a transition whose output spec is a single leaf is not checked for a write to that place either.
While the option is enabled they do not apply: a firing that ends with its action deposits the action's write whether or not it equals an output branch.
The option skips nothing else.
A write to a place the transition does not declare as an output still fails ([CORE-063]).
The build-time checks of [IO-011], [IO-012], [IO-013] and [IO-014] run when the transition is built, before any executor exists, and no executor option reaches them.
When enabled, output tokens are deposited without validation.
assumes: The model is the firing relation F of one executor that has the option and has it enabled, each firing read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire, Deposit); timing and priority play no part. The action may write any tokens into the transition's output places, so 'deposit the tokens an action wrote without validating them' is read as: every such write is the deposit of some firing (the first two lines). Deposits are compared per place (CORE-036), so several tokens in one place are one more such write.

'The skip covers the whole spec, its Place and ForwardInput leaves included' is why the first line ranges over every output spec: a transition whose output spec is Place(P) also fires with a write that misses P (CONC_026_forbids_leafValidated).

'It also covers the join-relay check of [NU-054] and the multiplicity warning of [IO-016] AC4, both of which run as part of validation.': a correlation name and a diagnostic are below the token-count granularity of the firing semantics; not encoded.

The paragraph naming IO-010, IO-011, IO-012, the per-firing check of IO-015 and the last two firing lines of CORE-036 is a scope: those blocks describe an executor with output validation enabled (their scope strings say so), and this block describes the executor with the option enabled. Theorem CONC_026_scoped shows both hold at once, each of its own executor, and that every firing of the validating executor on a transition that builds is a firing of the skipping one.

'The option skips nothing else' and 'A write to a place the transition does not declare as an output still fails ([CORE-063])' are the third line: a write outside the output places is not the deposit of any firing.

'A firing that ends with the timeout outcome deposits what [IO-013] and [IO-014] say.' is those blocks' subject, over the relation of timed-out firings; it is not restated here. A timeout deposit writes only output places, so the first line covers it.

'The build-time checks ... no executor option reaches them' is the fourth line: a transition that does not build (glossary: Builds) is not a transition any executor holds, so it never fires, the option enabled or not.

The first sentence's MAY (whether an executor offers the option at all), 'for known-correct nets' and the performance sentence are not encoded: the block describes an executor that offers the option, with it enabled. The implementation notes are not normative.
AC1 (the option is opt-in, validation is on by default) is about the builder's default, not about the firing relation; not encoded.
AC2 (when enabled, output tokens are deposited without validation) is the first two lines.
AC3 (when disabled, validation behaves identically to the bitmap executor) is the plain firing relation's subject (IO-010 to IO-015); not encoded here.
AC4 (Place(P) writing nothing, And(A, B) writing only A, both deposited) is the first two lines; CONC_026_nonvacuous fires both under the witness.
AC5 (no NU-054 diagnostic, no IO-016 AC4 warning) is below the token-count granularity; not encoded.
AC6 (a write to an undeclared place still fails, and building a transition that IO-012 rejects still fails) is the third and fourth lines.

requirements.title: Transition enablement
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N),
    Builds t →
      (while fun m ↦ ∃ s ∈ t.core.inputs, m s.place < requiredCount s.card, never
          Fire F t) ∧
        (while fun m ↦ ∃ p, ReadArc t p ∧ ¬Marked m p, never Fire F t) ∧
          (while fun m ↦ ∃ p, InhibitorArc t p ∧ Marked m p, never Fire F t) ∧
            ∀ (m : CountMarking N), Enabled t m → ∃ m', Fire F t m m'
reading: For every transition t that builds (Builds t: at most one input arc per place, no place twice in one output branch, at most one Timeout node, no Xor node inside the Timeout child, no ForwardInput outside a Timeout child, every forward's from an input place, no two output branches claiming the same set of places):
t does not fire from a marking in which the place of some input arc of t holds fewer tokens than that arc's required count;
t does not fire from a marking in which some read place of t is unmarked;
t does not fire from a marking in which some inhibitor place of t is marked;
from every marking m in which t is enabled, t fires to some marking m'.
quotes: A transition is **enabled** in a marking when every input place holds at least its required count (see [IO-001]–[IO-004]), every read place is marked and no inhibitor place is marked.
*While* an input place of a transition holds fewer tokens than its required count, the transition *shall not* fire.
*While* a read place of a transition is unmarked, the transition *shall not* fire.
*While* an inhibitor place of a transition is marked, the transition *shall not* fire.
*While* a transition is enabled, the transition *shall* be able to fire.

This requirement concerns transitions that build. A definition that building the transition rejects ([CORE-030], [IO-011]–[IO-014]) is not a transition of any net and is never enabled anywhere; in particular an output spec whose alternatives no write can tell apart ([IO-012]) never reaches a marking.
assumes: A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Enabled' is the glossary term (`Enabled`, readable form `enabled_iff`); 'can fire' / 'able to fire' is read as 'some firing exists'. The last line says a firing exists, not that an executor performs it now: when an enabled transition actually fires is the subject of the timing and scheduling requirements (TIME-*, EXEC-*).

Enablement is a function of the current marking alone: the three 'shall not' lines forbid a firing from every marking in which a condition fails, whatever happened before. This is how 'when any condition ceases to hold, the transition becomes disabled' of the previous wording is read.

The input condition ranges over every input arc of t, not only the first one per place. Under CORE-030 a transition has at most one input arc per place, so the two readings coincide on every transition that can be built.

The 'able to fire' line needs every transition to have at least one way to end (an output branch, or the empty deposit when it has no output spec); the reference semantics has one for every output spec (`Reference.exists_deposit`).
Transitions with a ν match specification (NU-020) add a correlation condition on top of these three; this block reads CORE-022 for transitions without one, as the reference semantics has none.
The inhibitor line restates the first clause of CORE-031 because CORE-022 lists it as one of its conditions; it is kept so that this block stands on its own.

'Transitions that build' is read as the build-time checks themselves (`Builds`): the input-arc check of CORE-030 and the output-spec checks of IO-011 (a place twice in one branch), IO-013 (more than one Timeout node), IO-014 (a ForwardInput outside a Timeout child; a forward from a non-input place) and IO-012 (two output branches claiming the same set of places). A transition that fails one constrains nothing here: no executor ever holds it, so it neither fires nor is required to. Branch sets are compared as sets (`SameSet`), so Xor(And(A, B, C), And(A, B)) and Xor(And(P, A), And(P, B)) build and are covered, while Xor(P, P) and Xor(And(A, B), And(B, A)) are not.
The reference `Out` is binary; n-ary And / Xor are read as right-nested, which keeps the IO-016 enumeration order, so the IO-012 branch indices and the build verdict are those of the n-ary spec.
AC1 (satisfied inputs, reads present, inhibitors empty, enabled) is the last line.
AC2 (missing input tokens, disabled) is the second line.
AC3 (missing read tokens, disabled) is the third line.
AC4 (inhibitor place has tokens, disabled) is the fourth line.

requirements.title: Input arc
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N) (c : Card),
    InputPlacesDistinct t →
      InputArc t p c →
        ¬ResetArc t p →
          ∀ (d : List N),
            on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun m m' ↦
              requiredCount c ≤ TokenCount m p →
                TokenCount m' p + consumptionCount c (TokenCount m p) =
                    TokenCount m p + Deposits d p ∧
                  (¬OutputArc t p →
                    TokenCount m' p + consumptionCount c (TokenCount m p) =
                      TokenCount m p)
reading: For every transition t that declares at most one input arc per place, every input place p of t whose input arc has cardinality c, p not a reset place of t, and every deposit d, every firing of t from m to m' depositing d, from a marking in which p holds at least the arc's required count:
leaves m'(p) + consumptionCount(c, m(p)) = m(p) + (the tokens d deposits in p): the firing removes exactly the consumption count from p, besides what it deposits there;
and, if p is not an output place of t either, leaves m'(p) + consumptionCount(c, m(p)) = m(p): p ends holding exactly the consumption count fewer tokens, whatever deposit the firing reports.
quotes: *When* a transition fires, it *shall* consume from each of its input places that is not also one of its reset places ([CORE-034]) as many tokens as the input arc's consumption count ([IO-001]–[IO-004], [IO-007]), oldest first.

*When* a transition fires, each of its input places that is neither one of its reset places nor one of its output places *shall* end the firing holding exactly the consumption count of its input arc fewer tokens than it held before the firing.
assumes: A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking with its deposit (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. Markings are token counts (glossary: Marking).

AC1 (a transition with an input arc consumes tokens from the place on firing) is the second line, with the amount the consumption count of the arc's cardinality; the third line is the second quoted sentence.
AC2 (consumed tokens follow FIFO order) and 'oldest first' are not encoded: which tokens leave a place is below the token-count granularity of the firing relation.

AC3 and the sentence 'If a transition declares two input arcs on the same place, building the transition shall fail with a descriptive error that names the transition and the place and suggests a single arc with `exactly(n)` / `atLeast(n)` instead.' are not encoded: the firing model has no transition builder and no error values. They are read as a hypothesis instead: the requirement constrains only transitions whose input places are distinct (InputPlacesDistinct), the only ones AC3 lets any executor, state-class graph or verifier see. Firings of a transition with duplicate input arcs are left unconstrained here, as the spec says their consumption has no coherent semantics.

The build-time output-spec checks (IO-011 to IO-014) are not a hypothesis here: neither line depends on the output spec beyond which places it names, so both hold of every transition with distinct input places, whether or not its output spec builds.

A place that is both an input place and a reset place of t is excluded by both quoted sentences: CORE-034 says such a place ends the firing holding exactly what was deposited there, so it is CORE-034's to constrain (the third hypothesis, ¬ ResetArc t p).
Interpretation: the consumption is read additively, m'(p) + consumed = m(p) + deposited, so a firing that also deposits into its own input place is counted correctly.

The deposit a firing reports is not trusted for the count on a place the output spec does not name (glossary: Output arc): no firing of t can deposit there ([CORE-035]), so the consumption shows in the marking alone, as the third line says. Without it a firing that consumes nothing but reports a deposit equal to the consumption count in its input place would pass the second line. This is the guard IO-001 to IO-004 also carry, so each of those blocks stands alone.

Interpretation: both lines are required only of firings from a marking in which p holds at least the arc's required count. A firing from a marking where p holds fewer is not enabled (CORE-022, IO-005); whether such a firing may happen at all is those requirements' business, and CORE-030, which speaks only of how much a firing consumes, says nothing about it.
'The same place' is equality of place names (TypeScript, Rust, [CORE-002]); Java's name-and-type equality is not modelled.

requirements.title: Inhibitor arc
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),
    InhibitorArc t p →
      (while fun m ↦ Marked m p, never Fire F t) ∧
        ∀ (m : CountMarking N) (m' : N → ℕ),
          ¬Marked m p → (Fire F t m m' ↔ Fire F (withoutInhibitor t p) m m')
reading: For every transition t and every inhibitor place p of t:
t does not fire from a marking in which p is marked;
from a marking m in which p is unmarked, t fires to m' exactly when t without its inhibitor arcs on p fires from m to m'.
quotes: *While* an inhibitor place of a transition is marked, the transition *shall not* fire.
*While* an inhibitor place of a transition is unmarked, the inhibitor arc *shall not* affect whether the transition can fire.
assumes: A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Can fire' and 'enabled' are both read as 'some firing exists'.
AC1 (inhibitor place empty, enablement unaffected) is the second line: with p unmarked, removing the inhibitor arcs on p changes neither whether t fires nor where it leads.
AC2 (inhibitor place marked, transition disabled) is the first line.

AC3, first half (a firing consumes nothing through its inhibitor arcs): by the second line a firing of t from a marking with p unmarked is a firing of t without its arcs on p, so those arcs add nothing to what it consumes or produces; by the first line t does not fire when p is marked. AC3, second half: what a firing of another transition consumes through an input arc on p is CORE-030's subject, not this block's.

requirements.title: Read Arc
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),
    ReadArc t p →
      (while fun m ↦ ¬Marked m p, never Fire F t) ∧
        (∀ (m : CountMarking N) (m' : N → ℕ),
            Marked m p → (Fire F t m m' ↔ Fire F (withoutRead t p) m m')) ∧
          ((∀ (c : Card), ¬InputArc t p c) →
            ¬ResetArc t p →
              ∀ (m : N → ℕ) (d : List N) (m' : N → ℕ),
                F t m d m' → m' p = m p + Deposits d p)
reading: For every transition t and every read place p of t:
t does not fire from a marking in which p is unmarked;
from a marking m in which p is marked, t fires to m' exactly when t without its read arcs on p fires from m to m';
if t has no input arc and no reset arc on p, every firing of t from m that deposits d and leaves m' has m'(p) = m(p) + (tokens d puts in p).
quotes: *While* a read place of a transition is unmarked, the transition *shall not* fire.
*While* a read place of a transition is marked, the read arc *shall not* affect whether the transition can fire or the marking its firing leaves.

*When* a transition fires, each of its read places on which it has neither an input arc nor a reset arc *shall* end the firing with its token count before the firing plus the tokens the firing deposits there.
assumes: A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Can fire' and 'enabled' are both read as 'some firing exists'.
AC1 (read place must have tokens for enablement) is the second line.

AC2 (token remains in place after firing) is the fourth line, for a read place the transition neither consumes from nor resets. A place that is also an input place or a reset place of the same transition loses tokens through those arcs ([CORE-030], [CORE-034], [EXEC-013] AC4); the third line says the read arc adds nothing to that loss.

AC3 (action receives the read token value) is not encoded: the firing relation works on token counts and has no action or token values. Which token is read is [EXEC-012]'s subject, the context access [CORE-061]'s.
'Marked' is read as 'holds at least one token' (glossary: Marked), the spec's 'at least one token for enablement'.

AC2's 'token remains' is encoded at count level only. A firing that takes the read token out of p and puts it, or another token, back in the same step leaves the same counts and satisfies this statement, but moves the token to the FIFO tail and changes its timestamp. Token identity, FIFO position and timestamp are below the count granularity of the firing relation, as for CORE-030 AC2; they belong to [EXEC-012] ('both A and B remain after firing', the oldest is peeked), and no count-level block can catch the bug.

requirements.title: Read arc multi-reader
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦
  (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),
      ReadArc t p →
        ∀ (m : CountMarking N),
          Marked m p →
            (∃ m', Fire F (core033_withoutRead t p) m m') → ∃ m', Fire F t m m') ∧
    ∀ (t₁ t₂ : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),
      ReadArc t₁ p →
        ReadArc t₂ p →
          (∀ (c : Card), ¬InputArc t₁ p c) →
            ¬ResetArc t₁ p →
              on Fire F t₁, shall fun m m' ↦
                Marked m p →
                  (∃ m'', Fire F (core033_withoutRead t₂ p) m' m'') →
                    ∃ m'', Fire F t₂ m' m''
reading: For every transition t and every read place p of t, at every marking m in which p is marked:
if t without its read arcs on p can fire from m, then t can fire from m;
for every two transitions t₁, t₂ with read arcs on p, where t₁ has no input arc and no reset arc on p:
after every firing of t₁ from a marking m in which p is marked to m', if t₂ without its read arcs on p can fire from m', then t₂ can fire from m'.
quotes: *While* a place is marked, a read arc to that place *shall not* stop its transition from firing, so all transitions with read arcs to the place can be enabled simultaneously.

*When* a transition with a read arc to a marked place fires, and the transition has no input arc and no reset arc to that place, the read arc of any transition to that place *shall not* stop that transition from firing afterwards (no conflict), since read arcs do not consume tokens.
assumes: A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Can fire' and 'enabled' are both read as 'some firing exists', to any target marking.

AC1 (two readers both enabled when the place has tokens) is the first two lines: whether a firing relation lets t fire from m depends on t and m alone, so 'both enabled' is each enabled, and each reader's read arc on a marked p adds no condition. The text does not claim a reader fires with its other arcs unsatisfied, hence the comparison with the reader without its read arcs on p.

AC2 (both can fire without conflict) is read in the untimed interleaving: firing one reader does not take away, through p, the other reader's ability to fire (last two lines). Conflicts through other places (t₁ consuming an input of t₂, or depositing into an inhibitor place of t₂) are not this block's subject.

The restriction to a t₁ with no input arc and no reset arc on p is an interpretation choice: such a t₁ removes tokens from p (CORE-030, CORE-034; EXEC-012 allows a read arc and a reset arc on one place), so it can disable the other reader; the text's reason 'read arcs do not consume tokens' covers the read arcs only.
t₁ and t₂ may be the same transition: a reader firing twice in a row is covered too. In the untimed step model this is no stronger than the case of two transitions with the same arcs.
The read token's value reaching the action (CORE-032 AC3, EXEC-012) is below the count granularity and not this block's subject.

Both clauses assume p is marked: a reader firing from an empty read place is CORE-032 AC1 (its first clause), not this block's subject. A firing relation that ignores read arcs satisfies this block (CORE_033_allows_ignoresRead).

Clause 2 asks only that p stay marked for the other reader, which is what 'no conflict' needs. That a read leaves the count of p unchanged (apart from deposits) is CORE-032 AC2 (its third clause); the 'since read arcs do not consume tokens' of this text is that requirement's reason, not a second acceptance criterion here. A read that takes one token whenever two or more are present satisfies this block (CORE_033_allows_readTakesSurplus).

Each firing is one atomic step, so a read token held or reserved while the reader's action runs (taken at the start and put back at completion, or a per-place lock on read places), which would keep two readers from being in flight together, cannot be expressed here. In-flight concurrency of readers needs a start/complete step model (CONC, EXEC); a take-and-put read that reorders the FIFO queue is below count granularity (EXEC-012).

requirements.title: Reset arc
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),
    ResetArc t p →
      (∀ (d : List N),
          on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x m' ↦ TokenCount m' p = Deposits d p) ∧
        (∀ (d : List N),
            on fun m m'' ↦ F (withoutReset t p) m d m'', shall fun m x ↦
              ∃ d' m', F t m d' m' ∧ SamePerPlace d d') ∧
          ∀ (d : List N),
            on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun m m' ↦
              ∃ d' m'',
                F (withoutReset t p) m d' m'' ∧
                  SamePerPlace d d' ∧
                    ∀ (q : N), q ≠ p → TokenCount m' q = TokenCount m'' q
reading: For every transition t and every reset place p of t, writing t∖p for t without its reset arcs on p:
every firing of t that deposits d leaves p with exactly as many tokens as d puts in p, whatever p held before;

every firing of t∖p from a marking m that deposits d is matched by a firing of t from m whose deposit puts the same number of tokens in every place (a reset arc removes no deposit, and t fires wherever t∖p does);

every firing of t from m that deposits d is matched by a firing of t∖p from m whose deposit puts the same number of tokens in every place and that leaves every place other than p with the same token count (a reset arc adds no deposit, t∖p fires wherever t does, and the arc changes no other place).
quotes: *When* a transition fires, each of its reset places *shall* lose every token it held before the firing and end the firing holding exactly the tokens the firing deposited there.
A reset arc *shall not* affect whether its transition can fire, whether the reset place is marked or not.

A reset arc *shall not* change what its transition can deposit: from every marking, the transition and the same transition without its reset arcs *shall* be able to make exactly the same deposits, so a reset arc neither adds a deposit nor removes one.
A reset arc *shall not* change the token count of any place other than its own.
assumes: A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Can fire' is read as 'some firing exists', to any target marking: removing a reset arc changes where a firing leads, so the second sentence compares the existence of a firing, not its target. It is the existence half of the second and third lines taken together (`CORE_034_canFire`), so it has no line of its own.
Deposits are compared per place (CORE-036): two deposits that put the same number of tokens in every place are the same deposit, whatever their order (`SamePerPlace`).

AC1 (fires even if the reset place is empty) is the second line at a marking with p empty: the reset arc on p adds no condition, so t fires there whenever t∖p does. The text does not claim t fires with its other arcs unsatisfied.

AC2 (all tokens removed on firing) is the first line. A reset place that is also an output place keeps what the firing deposited there (glossary: Deposit); a reset place that is also an input place ends with the deposit too, whatever was consumed from it.
AC3 (no token requirement, no contribution to enablement) is the second and third lines at every marking, empty or marked.

AC4 (same deposits with and without the reset arc, compared per place; a reset arc on an output place neither adds nor removes an outcome) is the second line (no outcome removed) and the third line (no outcome added).

The third line is also the frame of a reset arc: it rules out a reset that also empties a place the transition has no arc to, and a reset whose removed tokens feed a Forward or timeout deposit (they are not consumed; IO-013/IO-014 forward only consumed tokens). It compares against the same transition without the arc rather than spelling out the whole marking change; the effect of the other arcs is CORE-030, CORE-031, CORE-032 and IO-013's subject.

The comparison is over firing relations, not over which output specs build: a transition and the same transition without its reset arcs have the same output spec, so the build-time checks of IO-011 to IO-014 accept both or neither.

Token counts only: which tokens are removed, and EXEC-003 AC5 (a reset later in the same firing pass leaves same-pass deposits in place) are below this granularity; that refinement is EXEC-003's subject, not this block's.

requirements.title: Output arc
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (d : List N),
    (on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x x_1 ↦
        ∀ (p : N), Produced d p → OutputArc t p) ∧
      (on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x m' ↦ ∀ (p : N), Deposits d p ≤ m' p) ∧
        on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun m m' ↦
          ∀ (p : N),
            (∀ (c : Card), ¬InputArc t p c) → ¬ResetArc t p → m' p = m p + Deposits d p
reading: For every transition t and every deposit d:
every firing of t that deposits d puts tokens only in places that t's output spec names;
every firing of t that deposits d leaves a marking in which every place holds at least as many tokens as d put there;
every firing of t that deposits d, from m to m', leaves every place p with no input arc and no reset arc of t holding m p plus what d put in p, no more and no less.
quotes: *When* a transition fires, it *shall* deposit tokens only in its output places, according to its output spec (see [IO-010]–[IO-015]).
*When* a transition fires, the marking the firing leaves *shall* hold every token the firing deposited.
*When* a transition fires, every place that is neither an input place nor a reset place of the transition *shall* change by exactly the tokens the firing deposited there.
assumes: A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking that deposits the tokens of one outcome (glossary: Fire, Deposit); timing and priority play no part. 'When the transition's action completes' is read as 'when the firing deposits', for every outcome: the timeout outcome ([IO-013]) also deposits only in places the output spec names (a Timeout child, a ForwardInput's `to`).

An output place is a place the transition's output spec names (glossary: Output arc), every Xor branch, Timeout child and ForwardInput `to` included. A transition with no output spec has no output place, so its firings deposit nothing.

Which output places one firing deposits in, and how many tokens, is the subject of [IO-010]–[IO-016] ('according to its output spec'), not of this block: a firing relation that never deposits satisfies CORE-035 and is ruled out by [IO-016].

The second line says only that the deposited tokens are in the resulting marking; the exact count of an input place is [CORE-030]'s and of a reset place [CORE-034]'s. A reset place that is also an output place ends holding exactly what was deposited, which satisfies the line.

The third line is the marking side of 'only in its output places': on every place [CORE-030] and [CORE-034] do not cover (a pure output place, a read-only or inhibitor-only place, a place with no arc), the firing adds exactly its deposit. A place the firing does not deposit in is therefore unchanged, and an output place keeps its earlier tokens (no overwrite, no double or deduplicated deposit). On read places this coincides with [CORE-032]'s third clause.
AC1 (after the transition fires, produced tokens appear in the output place) is the second line, with the first saying the place is an output place.
AC2 (output tokens carry the current timestamp): not encoded. The firing relation works on token counts and carries no token timestamps; timestamps are [CORE-011] and the timed semantics' subject.

requirements.title: Arc semantics summary
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N),
    (∀ (p : N) (c : Card),
        InputArc t p c → while fun m ↦ TokenCount m p < requiredCount c, never Fire F t) ∧
      (∀ (p : N), ReadArc t p → while fun m ↦ ¬Marked m p, never Fire F t) ∧
        (∀ (p : N), InhibitorArc t p → while fun m ↦ Marked m p, never Fire F t) ∧
          (∀ (m : CountMarking N), Enabled t m → ∃ m', Fire F t m m') ∧
            (∀ (d : List N) (p : N) (c : Card),
                InputArc t p c →
                  ¬ResetArc t p →
                    on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun m m' ↦
                      TokenCount m' p =
                        TokenCount m p - consumptionCount c (TokenCount m p) +
                          Deposits d p) ∧
              (∀ (d : List N) (p : N),
                  (∀ (c : Card), ¬InputArc t p c) →
                    ¬ResetArc t p →
                      on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun m m' ↦
                        TokenCount m' p = TokenCount m p + Deposits d p) ∧
                (∀ (d : List N) (p : N),
                    ResetArc t p →
                      on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x m' ↦
                        TokenCount m' p = Deposits d p) ∧
                  ∀ (d : List N),
                    on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun m x ↦
                      (∃ b, OutputBranch t b ∧ OnPlacesOf d b) ∨
                        ∃ d₀, TimeoutOutcome t (Consumes t m) d₀ ∧ SamePerPlace d d₀
requirements.scope: all executors; the outcome line with output validation enabled (CONC-026, the default)
reading: For every transition t:
t does not fire from a marking in which an input place p holds fewer tokens than the required count c of its input arc;
t does not fire from a marking in which a read place p is unmarked;
t does not fire from a marking in which an inhibitor place p is marked;
from every marking at which t is enabled, some firing of t exists (to some marking);
every firing of t that deposits d leaves an input place p that is not a reset place with what it held, minus the consumption count of its arc, plus what d puts in p;
every firing of t that deposits d leaves a place p that is neither an input place nor a reset place of t with what it held plus what d puts in p;
every firing of t that deposits d leaves a reset place p with exactly what d puts in p;

every firing of t from m that deposits d either puts one or more tokens in each place of some output branch b of t and none in any other place, or puts in every place as many tokens as some timeout outcome d₀ of t for what the firing consumed from m.
quotes: *While* an input place of the transition holds fewer tokens than the required count of its input arc, the transition *shall not* fire.
*While* a read place of the transition is unmarked, the transition *shall not* fire.
*While* an inhibitor place of the transition is marked, the transition *shall not* fire.
*While* the transition is enabled, it *shall* be able to fire, whatever its output places and reset places hold.
*When* the transition fires, each input place that is not a reset place *shall* lose the consumption count of its input arc, and gain what the firing deposits there.
*When* the transition fires, each place that is neither an input place nor a reset place *shall* lose no tokens, and gain what the firing deposits there.
*When* the transition fires, each reset place *shall* end holding exactly what the firing deposited there.

*When* the transition fires and the firing ends with its action, on an executor with output validation enabled ([CONC-026], the default), the places in which it deposits *shall* be exactly the places of one output branch of its output spec, each receiving one or more tokens.
*When* the transition fires and the firing ends with the timeout outcome, it *shall* deposit in every place as many tokens as the timeout outcome puts there ([IO-013], [IO-014]).
Deposits are compared per place: the order in which a firing deposits its tokens is not normative, and two deposits that put the same number of tokens in every place are the same deposit.
assumes: A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part, so 'produced on complete' (Output) and 'consumed / removed on fire' (Input, Reset) both land in the one step. 'Able to fire' is read as 'some firing exists', to any target marking.

Requires token? column. 'Yes' for an input arc is read as 'holds at least the required count' (glossary: Enabled, Required count), which is one token for One and All; 'Yes' for a read arc as 'marked'; 'No (blocks if present)' for an inhibitor arc as 'marked blocks'. The 'No' entries (output, reset, and the inhibitor arc while its place is unmarked) are read together as the fourth line: the table lists every token requirement, so a transition whose input, read and inhibitor arcs are all satisfied can fire whatever its output and reset places hold.

Consumes? column. 'Yes' for an input arc is read as the consumption count of IO-007 (glossary: Consumption count). 'No' for output, inhibitor and read arcs is the sixth line: a place that only those arcs touch loses nothing. 'Yes (all)' for a reset arc is the seventh line (glossary: Deposit): a reset place that is also an output place keeps what the firing deposited there, and a reset place that is also an input place ends with the deposit too, so the fifth line excludes reset places.

The fifth line uses truncated subtraction, as Seam.fireNC does; under the first line the subtraction never truncates, because a firing only starts when every input place holds at least its required count.

Effect column, Output ('Token produced on complete') is the outcome line, the last line of the reading, which reads the eighth, ninth and tenth sentences quoted together. A firing relation does not record how a firing ended. As IO-012 says, a firing ends with its action when it does not end with the timeout outcome, and a firing whose deposit puts in every place as many tokens as some timeout-outcome deposit of the transition from the same marking may have ended with the timeout outcome. So the eighth and ninth sentences are read as one disjunction: the deposit marks exactly the places of an output branch (eighth: the branch fixes which places receive tokens, one or more each, not how many; glossary: Output branch, Produced set), or it equals a timeout outcome per place (ninth: as many tokens in every place). A transition with no output spec has the one empty branch, so it deposits nothing. Read ('Token remains') is the sixth line. Inhibitor ('Disables transition') is the third line.

Tenth sentence (deposits are compared per place). Every line of the reading reads the deposit d only through Deposits d (the produced set of d is the set of places p with Deposits d p ≠ 0), so two deposits that put the same number of tokens in every place satisfy it alike and the order of d plays no part: core036_c8_perPlace shows it for the outcome line, and core036_perPlace_closed shows that closing any firing relation under per-place equal deposits keeps CORE-036. Lines 5 to 7 already compare per place.

The outcome line is scoped by CONC-026: F is read as the firing relation of an executor with output validation enabled, the default. With the CONC-026 skip enabled a firing that ends with its action deposits what the action wrote, as CONC-026 says, and the outcome line is not claimed of it; lines 1 to 7 hold of every executor.

TimeoutOutcome reads the first Timeout node in pre-order. A transition that builds holds at most one Timeout node and no ForwardInput outside a Timeout child (IO-013, IO-014), so that node's outcome is the timeout outcome. Transitions that building rejects (IO-011 to IO-014) are not transitions of any net (CORE-022); the statement still ranges over every Trans, and the reference semantics satisfies it for all of them, so it needs no well-formedness premise. That at most one output branch matches a deposit (IO-012) is not part of CORE-036: the outcome line asks for some branch.
Read, 'provides value': the value of the read token is not visible at token-count granularity; that the action receives it is CORE-032 AC3, not encoded here.
Input token order (FIFO, CORE-030 AC2) and output token timestamps (CORE-035 AC2, IO-014 AC5) are below token-count granularity and not encoded here.

AC1 (each arc type behaves exactly as described in the table) is the whole statement: one line per cell of the 'Requires token?' column (lines 1 to 4) and of the 'Consumes?' and 'Effect' columns (lines 5 to 7 and the outcome line), as laid out in the assumptions above.

AC2 (an action that writes two tokens into one place of the branch it satisfies fires, and the marking receives all of them) is CORE_036_allows_multi: CORE-036 holds of a firing relation in which t: a → and(b, c) fires with the write b, b, c, and that firing leaves 2 tokens in b and 1 in c. That such a write is deposited at all is IO-015 and IO-016 AC4; CORE-036 only has to allow it.

AC3 (two firings that deposit the same number of tokens in every place, in different orders, deposit the same outcome) is core036_c8_perPlace and core036_perPlace_closed, and concretely CORE_036_allows_multi: the write c, b, b of the same transition is allowed alike and leaves the same marking.
InputArc names the first input arc on a place (glossary: Input arc); CORE-030 rejects a transition with two input arcs on one place at build, so for every well-formed transition it is the only one.

requirements.title: Input One
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),
    InputArc t p Card.one →
      (while fun m ↦ ¬Marked m p, never Fire F t) ∧
        (∀ (m : CountMarking N),
            Marked m p →
              ((∃ m', Fire F t m m') ↔ ∃ m', Fire F (io001_withoutInput t p) m m')) ∧
          (¬ResetArc t p →
            ∀ (m : N → ℕ) (d : List N) (m' : N → ℕ),
              F t m d m' →
                m' p + 1 = m p + Deposits d p ∧ (¬OutputArc t p → m' p + 1 = m p))
reading: For every transition t and place p such that the input arc of t on p is One:
t does not fire from a marking in which p is unmarked;
from a marking in which p is marked, t can fire exactly when t without its input arc on p can fire;

unless p is also a reset place of t, every firing of t from m that deposits d and leaves m' has m'(p) + 1 = m(p) + d(p): p loses exactly 1 token, besides what the firing deposits there; and if p is not an output place of t either, m'(p) + 1 = m(p): p loses exactly 1 token, whatever deposit the firing reports.
quotes: `One(place)` is an input arc whose required count and consumption count are both 1.
*While* the input place of a `One` input arc is unmarked, the transition *shall not* fire.
*While* the input place of a `One` input arc is marked, the arc *shall not* affect whether the transition can fire.
*When* a transition with a `One` input arc fires, it *shall* consume exactly 1 token from the input place.

*When* a transition with a `One` input arc fires, and the input place is neither a reset place nor an output place of the transition, the input place *shall* end the firing holding exactly 1 fewer token than it held before the firing.
assumes: A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking with its deposit (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Can fire' and 'enables' are both read as 'some firing exists'.

The first quoted sentence and the bullets (`requiredCount()` returns 1, `consumptionCount(available)` returns 1) are IO-007's contract for `One`. Here it is observed through firing: the required count is the second and third lines, the consumption count the fourth. The bullet values themselves are `io001_counts`.

AC1 (enables when the place has >= 1 token) is the second line (not with 0 tokens) and the third line (with >= 1 token the arc does not stand in the way; whether the other arcs allow the firing is theirs to say, IO-005 and CORE-022).

AC2 (exactly 1 token consumed on firing) is the fourth line for the count. Which token is consumed (the oldest) is below the count granularity of the firing semantics and is the glossary's reading of Consume (CORE-030); it is not encoded here.
AC3 (remaining tokens stay in the place) is the fourth line: p holds m(p) - 1 tokens plus the firing's deposit there afterwards.

Consumption is observed through the marking: p loses 1 and gains what the firing deposits there (p may also be an output place). A place that is both the input place and a reset place of t ends holding what the firing deposited there (CORE-034), so the consumed token is not visible in the marking; the fourth line excludes that case.

The deposit a firing reports is not trusted for the count: on a place that t's output spec does not name (glossary: Output arc) no firing of t can deposit ([CORE-035]), so there the consumed token shows in the marking alone, as exactly 1 token fewer. Without this a firing that consumes nothing but reports a deposit of 1 in the input place would pass the count.
The input arc of t on p is the first input arc on p (glossary: Input arc), and t without its input arc on p drops that arc only; CORE-030 rejects a second input arc on p at build.

requirements.title: Input Exactly
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N) (n : ℕ),
    InputArc t p (Card.exactly n) →
      (while fun m ↦ TokenCount m p < n, never Fire F t) ∧
        (¬ResetArc t p →
          ∀ (m : N → ℕ) (d : List N) (m' : N → ℕ),
            F t m d m' →
              m' p + n = m p + Deposits d p ∧ (¬OutputArc t p → m' p + n = m p))
reading: For every transition t, place p and count N such that the input arc of t on p is Exactly(N):
t does not fire from a marking in which p holds fewer than N tokens;

unless p is also a reset place of t, every firing of t from m that deposits d and leaves m' has m'(p) + N = m(p) + d(p): p loses exactly N tokens, besides what the firing deposits there; and if p is not an output place of t either, m'(p) + N = m(p): p loses exactly N tokens, whatever deposit the firing reports.
quotes: `Exactly(place, n)` is an input arc whose required count and consumption count are both N, where N >= 1.
*While* the input place of an `Exactly(n)` input arc holds fewer than N tokens, the transition *shall not* fire.
*When* a transition with an `Exactly(n)` input arc fires, it *shall* consume exactly N tokens from the input place.

*When* a transition with an `Exactly(n)` input arc fires, and the input place is neither a reset place nor an output place of the transition, the input place *shall* end the firing holding exactly N fewer tokens than it held before the firing.
assumes: A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking with its deposit (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Enables' is read as 'some firing exists'.

The first quoted sentence (required count N, consumption count N; the bullets `requiredCount()` returns N and `consumptionCount(available)` returns N) is IO-007's contract for `Exactly(n)`. Here it is observed through firing: the required count is the second line, the consumption count the third. The bullets' qualifier 'when available >= N' is implied: by the second line no firing starts with fewer.

AC1 (construction with N < 1 rejected, also when the transition is built from a spec written out without the constructor): a property of construction, not of firing, so the formula does not encode it. The formula quantifies over every N, N = 0 included; for N = 0 both lines hold of the reference semantics trivially, so the restriction N >= 1 neither weakens nor strengthens what is checked about firing.

AC2 (enables only when the place has >= N tokens) and AC4 (N-1 tokens, not enabled) are the second line. The converse ('enables when the place has >= N tokens', given the other arcs allow it) is the AND-join of IO-005 and CORE-022, not this block's subject.

AC3 (exactly N consumed on firing, the N oldest, FIFO) is the third line for the count; its second part (the fourth quoted sentence) states it without the deposit for an input place that is neither a reset place nor an output place. Which tokens are consumed (the oldest, FIFO) is below the count granularity of the firing semantics and is the glossary's reading of Consume (CORE-030); it is not encoded here.

Consumption is observed through the marking: p loses N and gains what the firing deposits there (p may also be an output place). A place that is both the input place and a reset place of t ends holding what the firing deposited there (CORE-034), so the N tokens consumed are not visible in the marking; the third line excludes that case, as the fourth quoted sentence does.

The deposit a firing reports is not trusted for the count: on a place that t's output spec does not name (glossary: Output arc) no firing of t can deposit ([CORE-035]), so there the consumed tokens show in the marking alone, as exactly N tokens fewer (the fourth quoted sentence, IO-001's guard). Without this a firing that consumes nothing but reports a deposit of N in the input place would pass the count, and the block would lean on CORE-035 to stand.

Deposits are counts per place (glossary: Deposit, [CORE-036]): `Deposits d p` counts the tokens d puts in p and ignores their order. The build-time output-spec checks of IO-011 to IO-014 (ambiguity, one Timeout, ForwardInput only under a Timeout) and the validation skip of CONC-026 do not touch input consumption, so the formula quantifies over every transition, built or not, and every executor.
The input arc of t on p is the first input arc on p (glossary: Input arc); CORE-030 rejects a second one at build.

requirements.title: Input All
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),
    AllArc t p →
      (while fun m ↦ ¬Marked m p, never Fire F t) ∧
        (∀ (m : CountMarking N),
            Marked m p → ((∃ m', Fire F t m m') ↔ ∃ m', Fire F (withoutAll t p) m m')) ∧
          (∀ (d : List N),
              on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x m' ↦ m' p = Deposits d p) ∧
            (¬OutputArc t p →
              ∀ (d : List N), on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x m' ↦ m' p = 0)
reading: For every transition t and every place p on which t has an `All` input arc:
t does not fire from a marking in which p is unmarked;
from a marking in which p is marked, t can fire exactly when t without its `All` input arcs on p can fire;
every firing of t that deposits d leaves p holding exactly the tokens d puts there;
if p is not an output place of t, every firing of t leaves p empty, whatever deposit the firing reports.
quotes: *While* the place of an `All` input arc of a transition is unmarked, the transition *shall not* fire.
*While* the place of an `All` input arc of a transition is marked, the `All` input arc *shall not* affect whether the transition can fire.
*When* a transition fires, it *shall* consume every token from the place of each of its `All` input arcs.
*When* a transition fires, the place of each of its `All` input arcs that is not an output place of the transition *shall* end the firing empty.
assumes: A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Can fire' is read as 'some firing to some marking exists'.
The first two lines together say that the `All` arc requires exactly one token: `requiredCount()` returns 1 (the first bullet; `Card.required .all = 1`).

'Consume every token' is read through the place's count after the firing: p ends holding only what this firing deposited in p, so it kept none of its own tokens. This is the second bullet, `consumptionCount(available)` returns `available`. A firing that also deposits into p (p is an output place of t) leaves those tokens in p.

AC1 (enables when the place has >= 1 token) is the second line: with p marked the `All` arc removes no firing. AC3 (0 tokens, not enabled) is the first line. AC2 (all tokens consumed, place empty after) is the third line, with 'empty' read as 'empty apart from this firing's own deposit into p', and the fourth line, where p is not an output place and 'empty' is literal.

The fourth line is the guard IO-001 also carries: it does not trust the deposit a firing reports. On a place that t's output spec does not name (glossary: Output arc) no firing can deposit (CORE-035, CORE-063), so there the drain shows in the marking alone, as an empty place. Without it, a firing that keeps p's tokens and reports them as its own deposit into p would pass the third line. The fourth line stands alone: it needs neither the third line nor CORE-035.

A reset arc on p does not weaken the fourth line: the spec sentence has no reset exclusion, and a reset place that is not an output place ends holding what the firing deposited there (CORE-034), which is nothing.
Deposits are compared per place (CORE-036): the lines read the count `Deposits d p` and the marking's count at p, never the order of d.
Which token is consumed first, and that the consumed tokens reach the action, are below the count granularity of a firing relation; they are not encoded.

A transition with two input arcs on p is rejected at build by CORE-030. On such a transition the formula reads the first arc on p, as the reference does (`InputArc`); `withoutAll` removes only the `All` arcs on p.

requirements.title: Input AtLeast
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N) (n : ℕ),
    InputArc t p (Card.atLeast n) →
      (while fun m ↦ TokenCount m p < n, never Fire F t) ∧
        (∀ (m : CountMarking N),
            n ≤ TokenCount m p →
              ((∃ m', Fire F t m m') ↔ ∃ m', Fire F (withoutInputArc t p) m m')) ∧
          (∀ (d : List N),
              on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x m' ↦ TokenCount m' p = Deposits d p) ∧
            (¬OutputArc t p →
              ∀ (d : List N),
                on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x m' ↦ TokenCount m' p = 0)
reading: For every transition t, place p and number n such that the input arc of t on p is AtLeast(p, n):
t does not fire from a marking in which p holds fewer than n tokens;
from a marking m in which p holds at least n tokens, t can fire from m exactly when t without its input arc on p can fire from m;
every firing of t, with whatever deposit d, leaves p holding exactly the tokens d deposited there (every token p held was consumed);
if p is not an output place of t, every firing of t leaves p empty, whatever deposit the firing reports.
quotes: *While* the input place of an `AtLeast(place, minimum)` input arc holds fewer than `minimum` tokens, the transition *shall not* fire.
*While* the input place of an `AtLeast(place, minimum)` input arc holds at least `minimum` tokens, the input arc *shall not* affect whether the transition can fire.
*When* a transition with an `AtLeast(place, minimum)` input arc fires, it *shall* consume every token the input place holds.
*When* a transition with an `AtLeast(place, minimum)` input arc fires, and the input place is not an output place of the transition, the input place *shall* end the firing empty.
assumes: A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Can fire' is read as 'some firing from m exists', whatever marking it leads to: removing the arc changes what the firing consumes from p, so only whether t fires is compared, not where it leads.

'The input arc on p' is the first input arc on p, as the glossary term Input arc reads it; `withoutInputArc` removes that one arc. [CORE-030] allows at most one input arc per place, so on a well-formed transition it is the only one.

AC1 (construction with minimum < 1 is rejected): not encoded. It is a build-time check on the net definition, outside the firing relation. The statement quantifies over every n, n = 0 included; the reference semantics satisfies it there too (AtLeast(p, 0) never blocks and drains p).

AC2 (transition enables when the place has >= minimum tokens) is the second line: with p holding at least n tokens the arc does not stop t from firing. Read with [IO-005], the other arcs of t still decide.

AC3 (all tokens consumed on firing, not just minimum) is the third line, stated on the marking the firing leaves: p ends holding what was deposited there and nothing it held before. A reset arc on p ([CORE-034]) gives the same end count, so neither the third nor the fourth line needs a reset guard.

The fourth line is the guard IO-001 carries, so the block stands alone: the deposit a firing reports is not trusted for the count. On a place the output spec of t does not name, no firing of t can deposit ([CORE-035]), so the drain shows in the marking alone, as an empty place. Without it a firing that consumes nothing but reports a deposit in p equal to what p held would pass the third line.
AC4 (place with minimum - 1 tokens, transition not enabled) is the first line, at the count minimum - 1.

The two bullets (`requiredCount()` returns `minimum`, `consumptionCount(available)` returns `available`) are the pure-function contract of [IO-007] and the glossary terms Required count and Consumption count; this block encodes their effect on firing (lines 1 to 4), not the functions themselves.

The output-spec build checks ([IO-011] to [IO-014]) and the output validation skip ([CONC-026]) do not touch input consumption; the block holds of every firing relation over every transition, built or not.

requirements.title: Input AND-Join Semantics
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N),
    (∀ s ∈ t.core.inputs,
        while fun m ↦ TokenCount m s.place < requiredCount s.card, never Fire F t) ∧
      ∀ (m : CountMarking N),
        (∀ s ∈ t.core.inputs, requiredCount s.card ≤ TokenCount m s.place) →
          ((∃ m', Fire F t m m') ↔ ∃ m', Fire F (withoutInputs t) m m')
reading: For every transition t:
for every input arc s of t, t does not fire from a marking in which the input place of s holds fewer tokens than the required count of s;
from a marking m in which every input place of t holds at least the required count of its input arc, t can fire from m exactly when t without its input arcs can fire from m.
quotes: *While* any input place of a transition holds fewer tokens than the required count of its input arc, the transition *shall not* fire.
*While* every input place of a transition holds at least the required count of its input arc, the input arcs *shall not* affect whether the transition can fire.
assumes: A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Can fire' and 'enabled' are both read as 'some firing exists' (to some marking): the input arcs change what a firing consumes, so the second line compares whether t fires, not where it leads.
'Simultaneously satisfied' is read as 'satisfied in the one marking the firing starts from': both lines fix a single marking m.
Input arcs are read from the transition's list of input arcs, every one of them. A transition with two input arcs on one place, which [CORE-030] rejects at build, is gated by both.

AC1 (a transition with 3 inputs enables only when all 3 places have sufficient tokens) is the first line, for any number of input arcs, 3 included; the test derivation's 'satisfy all 3; verify enabled' is the second line together with a transition that, without its input arcs, can fire (no read or inhibitor arc blocks it).
AC2 (any one input unsatisfied disables the transition) is the first line.
How many tokens an input arc requires (requiredCount) is IO-001 to IO-004 and IO-007, not this block: the statement takes requiredCount as given.

requirements.title: requiredCount and consumptionCount Contract
requirements.statement:
fun K ↦
  (∀ (c : Card),
      K.required c =
        match c with
        | Card.one => 1
        | Card.exactly n => n
        | Card.all => 1
        | Card.atLeast m => m) ∧
    (∀ (c : Card) (a : ℕ),
        K.required c ≤ a →
          K.consume c a =
            some
              (match c with
              | Card.one => 1
              | Card.exactly n => n
              | Card.all => a
              | Card.atLeast n => a)) ∧
      ∀ (c : Card), ∀ a < K.required c, K.consume c a = none
reading: requiredCount() is 1 for One, n for Exactly(n), 1 for All and m for AtLeast(m);
for every cardinality c and every available ≥ requiredCount(c), consumptionCount(available) returns 1 for One, n for Exactly(n), available for All and available for AtLeast(m);
for every cardinality c and every available < requiredCount(c), consumptionCount(available) fails (none).
quotes: The required count *shall* be 1 for `One` and `All`, `n` for `Exactly(n)` and `m` for `AtLeast(m)`.
*While* `available` is at least the required count, `consumptionCount(available)` *shall* return 1 for `One`, `n` for `Exactly(n)` and `available` for `All` and `AtLeast(m)`.
*If* `consumptionCount(available)` is called with `available` less than the required count, *then* the call *shall* fail with an error.
assumes: A contract is the pair of functions of one implementation; a call that raises (an exception, a panic, an assertion failure) is read as `none`, a call that returns `k` as `some k`. Which error is raised, and its message, are not part of the statement.
AC1 (each variant returns the values of the table) is the first two lines: the first line is the requiredCount column, the second the consumptionCount column on every call the third line allows.
AC2 (calling consumptionCount with insufficient tokens is an error) is the third line.
The counts n and m range over all naturals. That Exactly(n) and AtLeast(m) are built only with n, m ≥ 1 is IO-002 AC1 and IO-004 AC1, not this block's subject; the table holds for 0 too.

'(matching) tokens' in the definition of requiredCount() is read at the granularity of a token count: which tokens of a place count as matching (the ν correlation of NU-020) is decided before the count reaches these functions, so `available` is already the matching count.

That an executor calls consumptionCount only on an enabled transition, where every input place holds its required count, is enablement (CORE-022, IO-005), not this block's subject; that a firing removes exactly consumptionCount(available) tokens is CORE-030's subject (glossary: Consume, bridge lemma `consumes_eq`).

requirements.title: Output place (leaf)
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),
    OutputSpec t = some (Out.place p) →
      ∀ (d : List N),
        (on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x x_1 ↦ Produced d p) ∧
          (on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x x_1 ↦ ∀ (q : N), Produced d q → q = p) ∧
            on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun m m' ↦
              (if ResetArc t p then 0 else TokenCount m p - Consumes t m p) +
                  Deposits d p ≤
                TokenCount m' p
requirements.scope: executors with output validation enabled (the default)
reading: For every transition t whose output spec is the leaf Place(p), and every deposit d:
every firing of t that deposits d puts at least one token in p;
every firing of t that deposits d puts no token in any place other than p;
every firing of t that deposits d, from m to m', leaves p holding at least what p kept (nothing if t has a reset arc on p, else m p minus what t consumed from p) plus what d put in p.
quotes: `Place(place)` is a leaf node of an output spec that names a single output place.
*When* a transition whose output spec is `Place(place)` fires, it *shall* deposit one or more tokens in `place`.
*When* a transition whose output spec is `Place(place)` fires, it *shall not* deposit a token in any other place.

*When* a transition whose output spec is `Place(place)` fires, the marking the firing leaves *shall* hold in `place` the tokens the firing deposited there, in addition to the tokens `place` kept through the firing.
This requirement applies to an executor with output validation enabled, which is the default ([CONC-026]).
assumes: The firing relation F is that of an executor with output validation enabled, the default (CONC-026). An executor with the CONC-026 skip enabled deposits whatever the action wrote, its Place leaf included, so it may write nothing; CONC-026 lifts IO-010 for it, and the evidence below shows that such an executor's firing relation (io010_skipFire) does not satisfy IO-010 (IO_010_forbids_skip), which is why the scope is stated.

A transition whose output spec is the leaf Place(p) passes every build-time check of its output spec (IO-011 to IO-014: one place, no Timeout, no ForwardInput, one output branch), so the statement ranges over transitions that build; no well-formedness hypothesis is needed.

A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking that deposits the tokens of one outcome (glossary: Fire, Deposit); timing and priority play no part. A completion that fails, by an action exception or by IO-015 validation, deposits no outcome and is not a firing here.

The statement covers a transition whose whole output spec is the leaf. A Place leaf inside And, Xor or Timeout contributes its claim {place} to an output branch (IO-015); what that branch must receive is the subject of IO-011, IO-012, IO-013 and IO-015, not of this block.

'One or more tokens' is read on the deposit (glossary: Produced set): p is in the produced set. How many tokens beyond one is not constrained: an output branch is a set of places, and several tokens into p conform (IO-015, IO-016 AC4, CORE-036); the reference semantics deposits exactly one (IO-016). Deposits are compared per place (Deposits d p, Produced d p), never by list order (CORE-036).
The second clause (nothing outside p) reads 'a single output place' together with IO-015's exact-explanation rule: the produced set of a firing of a Place(p) spec is exactly {p}.

AC1 (output spec declares a single place) is structural and holds by construction: the leaf names one place, outPlaces (Place p) = [p] (checked by example below); the statement's hypothesis selects exactly these transitions.

AC2 (produced tokens appear in the place) is the first clause on the deposit and the third clause on the marking. The third clause is a lower bound: it rules out a lost write (the firing reports [p] but leaves p as it was) and a misrouted write (the token lands in another place), also when p already holds tokens. The exact count of p (no extra tokens) is [CORE-030]'s on an input place, [CORE-034]'s on a reset place and [CORE-035]'s third line on every other place; tokens appearing in other places are [CORE-035]'s.

'The tokens place kept' is the glossary's effect of a firing on one place: a reset place keeps none [CORE-034], an input place keeps its count minus the consumption count [CORE-030], [IO-007], any other place keeps its count. Inhibitor and read arcs consume nothing [CORE-031], [CORE-032].

requirements.title: Output And
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] [ToString N] Build F ↦
  (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (o : Out N),
      OutputSpec t = some o →
        DupBranch o →
          Build t ≠ none ∧
            (InputsDistinct t →
              ∀ (p : N), firstDup o = some p → Build t = some (msgDup t p))) ∧
    ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (l r : Out N),
      OutputSpec t = some (l.and r) →
        Builds t →
          (l.and r).findTimeout = none →
            (∀ c ∈ andChildren (l.and r),
                ∀ (d : List N),
                  on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x x_1 ↦ ChildReceived d c) ∧
              ∀ (d : List N),
                on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x x_1 ↦
                  IO_011_uniqueBranch (l.and r) d
requirements.scope: executors with output validation enabled (the default, CONC-026)
reading: Let Build be the builder (Build t = none: t builds; Build t = some msg: building t fails with msg) and F the firings.

For every transition t whose output spec o names a place twice in one output branch (DupBranch), building t fails; and if t's input places are distinct, it fails with IO-011's message for t and the place p the walk of o reports (firstDup o = some p, msgDup t p).
For every transition t that builds (Builds) whose output spec is an And node o with no Timeout node in it:
for every child c of o (nested Ands flattened) and every deposit d, every firing of t that deposits d produces some place that c names;

for every deposit d, every firing of t that deposits d has as its produced set, on the places o names, exactly the places of the output branch at one index of o's branch list, and of no branch at any other index (IO_011_uniqueBranch).
F is the firing relation of an executor with output validation enabled.
quotes: `And(children)` is a node of an output spec that represents a parallel fork in which all children are active.

*When* a transition whose output spec is `And(children)` fires and its action completes, every child, with nested `And`s flattened, *shall* have received tokens: the produced set contains a place that the child names.
The same holds for an `And` nested in the alternative that an inner `Xor` chose: the produced set *shall* equal, on the places the output spec names, one output branch of the output spec.
That output branch is unique, because the output branches of a spec that builds are pairwise distinct sets ([IO-012]).
This requirement applies to an executor with output validation enabled, which is the default ([CONC-026]).
*If* a single output branch (one choice at every `Xor`, with nested `And`s flattened) names the same place twice, *then* the output spec *shall* be rejected, with

*If* the output spec names a place twice in one output branch, *then* `

` in the message *shall* be the place that the following walk of the spec reports first, so that every implementation names the same place:
A `Place(P)` node and a `ForwardInput(from, P)` node name `P`.
A `Timeout` node walks its child and names the places its child names.
An `Xor` node walks its children left to right.
*If* a child reports a place, *then* the `Xor` *shall* report that place.
Otherwise the `Xor` names the places its children name, each once, in the order the walk first meets them.
An `And` node walks its children left to right.
*If* a child reports a place, *then* the `And` *shall* report that place.
Otherwise, *if* a place the child names, taken in the order the walk first met them, is already named by an earlier child, *then* the `And` *shall* report the first such place.
Otherwise the `And` names the places its children name, each once, in the order the walk first meets them.
The walk reports a place exactly when some output branch names a place twice, because the alternatives of an `Xor` under an `And` are chosen independently of the `And`'s other children.
assumes:
The model is the pair (Build, F). Build is the transition builder, read as the message building a transition fails with, none when it builds; the witness is the reference builder refBuild, which runs the build-time checks of the Output Composition preamble in order (glossary: Build-time checks). The build error is msgDup, byte for byte: the message of the paragraph 'A place at most once per branch' with the transition's name and

the place the walk reports. The preamble does not place the CORE-030 input-arc check among the output-spec checks; refBuild runs it first, so on a transition with two input arcs on one place the build line only requires that building fails.

The walk is firstDup, through dupScan, clause for clause: steps 1 and 2 are its place, forward and timeout clauses, step 3 its xor clause (xorJoin: the first child's report, else the second's, else the places of both, each once, in first-seen order), step 4 its and clause (andStep at each child: the child's report, else the first place the child names that an earlier child of the And names, else the child's places join the pool). The reference Out is binary: an n-ary And or Xor is right-nested, and dupScan walks a .and met as a child of a .and as part of its parent, so the children of And(c1, ..., cn) are walked as the n-ary node's children. A spec with an And written as a direct child of an And is the one shape the binary Out cannot tell from the flat n-ary node; on it the builders walk the inner And first, the loader's walk (Load.dupWalk, over the spec as written) does the same, and firstDup reads the flat node.

'The walk reports a place exactly when some output branch names a place twice' is the theorem firstDup_eq_none_iff, and the place it reports is named twice in some output branch (firstDup_some); the build line therefore names a place exactly when it rejects a duplicate. AC5's And(Xor(A, B), Xor(B, A)) names B (IO_011_ac5); naming the first place repeated in the first repeating output branch, in IO-016 order, would name A, and that builder violates the build line (IO_011_forbids_firstBranchName).

'Which place the message names' is a constraint on the message only: which transitions build is the first build line together with the other build-time checks, and IO-013's third line ties Builds to the builder.

A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking that deposits the tokens of one outcome (glossary: Fire, Deposit); timing and priority play no part. A completion that fails validation (AC3) deposits no outcome and is not a firing here.

Scope: 'applies to an executor with output validation enabled' is read as a restriction on the model: F is the firing relation of such an executor. An executor with the CONC-026 skip enabled is not an F this block speaks of; what it does (an And(A, B) firing that deposits only A, CONC-026 AC4) is exactly what io011_leftOnlyFire models, and this block forbids it of a validating executor (IO_011_forbids_leftOnly).

Scope: the statement quantifies over transitions that build. Building runs the checks of the Output Composition preamble (WellFormedOut: no place twice in one output branch, at most one Timeout node, no Xor node inside the Timeout child, no ForwardInput outside a Timeout child, every ForwardInput's from an input place, no two output branches at different indices with the same set of places). CORE-022 applies to transitions that build, and a definition the checks reject is not a transition of any net. Build reads one transition definition, so the construction paths that reach the builder are not encoded.

The reference semantics reads an n-ary And as right-nested binary `Out.and` nodes; `andChildren` flattens them back, so the children of And(A, B, C) are A, B and C. Flattening is the recursive reading of 'ALL child output specs must receive tokens': a nested And has received tokens exactly when each of its own children has.

'Received tokens' and 'the produced set' are read on the set of places the deposit touches (Produced, membership in d), and an output branch is read as a set of places (glossary: Output branch): several tokens into one place of the chosen branch conform, and the order of the deposit plays no part (CORE-036). How many tokens is IO-016's subject. Places outside the output spec are not constrained here (CORE-035 ties the marking to the deposit).

'Fires and its action completes' is read on output specs with no Timeout node (findTimeout = none), where every firing ends with its action. An output spec with its one Timeout node anywhere in it, such as And(A, Timeout(d, B)), is IO-013's: the deposit alone cannot tell the timeout outcome from the action outcome, so this block does not restate it there.

The second clause is the recursive reading of 'ALL children receive tokens' below an Xor: an And under the Xor alternative the action chose must give every one of its children tokens, and the Xor itself must take one alternative (IO-012). Without it a deposit [0, 3] for And(Xor(And(0, 1), 2), 3) (a partial write of the chosen alternative) and a deposit [0, 1, 2] for And(0, Xor(1, 2)) (both alternatives) satisfy the first clause.

'That output branch is unique' is read by index: one entry of the IO-016 branch list, one per assignment. On a transition that builds it follows from the existence half and the last build check (IO_011_unique_of_wf), so it adds no constraint on F beyond the scope; no weaker mutant can tell it apart, and the evidence for it is that lemma and IO_011_reference_ambiguous, which shows that without the scope the reference fires And(Q, Xor(P, P)) with two exact branches.
AC1 (requires at least 1 child) is structural and not encoded: the reference output spec has binary And nodes only, so an And with no child cannot be written; an And with one child is that child.
AC2 (after the action completes, all children have received tokens) is the first clause, and the second at every depth.

AC3 (validation failure if a child received no tokens) is read on firings: a completion in which a child received no tokens is not a firing, so the marking never shows it. That the failure is reported (an ActionFailed outcome, the error the user sees) is not observable in the firing relation, which has no events or errors; it is EXEC-030's and IO-015's subject and is not encoded here.

AC4 and the paragraph 'A place at most once per branch' are the build line, and the first build check of WellFormedOut (every output branch Nodup, equivalently no BranchDuplicate, IO_011_noDuplicate_of_wf) for the firing lines' scope: And(P, P), And(P, And(Q, P)) and Xor(A, And(P, P)) are rejected with the message naming P, and Xor(And(P, A), And(P, B)) builds (IO_011_ac4). The construction paths and MOD-020's more specific message are not in the model. The reference semantics still fires And(P, P) depositing two tokens in P (IO_011_reference_fires_duplicate); that transition does not build, so the firing lines do not speak of it.
AC5 (And(Xor(A, B), Xor(B, A)) is rejected naming B) is the build line on that spec, checked under the reference builder (IO_011_ac5).

requirements.title: Output Xor
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] [ToString N] C Build F ↦
  (∀ (o : Out N), C o = none ↔ IO_012_unambiguous o) ∧
    (∀ (o : Out N) (i j : ℕ) (ps : List N),
        C o = some (i, j, ps) ↔ IO_012_reported o i j ps) ∧
      (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (o : Out N),
          OutputSpec t = some o →
            ¬IO_012_unambiguous o →
              Build t ≠ none ∧
                (InputsDistinct t →
                  ¬DupBranch o →
                    timeoutCount o ≤ 1 →
                      xorInTimeout o = false →
                        forwardOutside o = none →
                          (∀ s ∈ forwardSources o, s ∈ inPlaces t) →
                            ∀ (i j : ℕ) (ps : List N),
                              C o = some (i, j, ps) →
                                Build t = some (msgAmbiguous t i j ps))) ∧
        ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (l r : Out N),
          OutputSpec t = some (l.xor r) →
            IO_012_unambiguous (l.xor r) →
              ∀ (d : List N),
                on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m' ∧ ¬IO_012_timeoutLike t m d, shall fun x x_1 ↦
                  ∃ b ∈ (l.xor r).branches, ExactOn (l.xor r) d b
requirements.scope: build check: every transition, on every construction path; firing lines: executors with output validation enabled (the default, CONC-026)
reading: Build check. For every output spec o (the output spec of the transition being built), with bs its output branches (Out.branches, one entry per assignment, numbered from 0):
the check C passes (C o = none) exactly when no two entries of bs at indices i < j claim the same set of places (IO_012_unambiguous; IO_012_clash compares the entries as sets, SameSet);

the check fails reporting (i, j, ps) (C o = some (i, j, ps)) exactly when the entries i < j clash, no entry before j clashes with an earlier one, no entry before i clashes with entry j, and ps is entry i as a list (IO_012_reported).

Building. For every transition t whose output spec o is ambiguous (not IO_012_unambiguous): building t fails (Build t ≠ none); and when every earlier build-time check passes (input places distinct, CORE-030; no output branch naming a place twice, IO-011; at most one Timeout node and no Xor node inside its child, IO-013; no ForwardInput outside a Timeout child and every forward from an input place, IO-014), building fails with IO-012's message for the pair (i, j) and the places ps the check reports (msgAmbiguous t i j ps).

Firing. For every transition t whose output spec is Xor(l, r) and passes the check, every deposit d, and every firing of t under F from m to m' that deposits d and whose deposit is not, place by place, a timeout-outcome deposit of t from m (IO_012_timeoutLike): some output branch b of Xor(l, r) is exact for d: on every place q the output spec names, d puts one or more tokens in q exactly when q is in b (ExactOn).

The second firing line is a consequence, not a clause: on an output spec that passes the check two exact branches would be the same set (both lie within outPlaces), so at most one is exact (theorem IO_012_unique).
`on R, shall Q` reads: every step from m to m' with R m m' satisfies Q m m'; here Q ignores both markings.
